messages:
anya: P95 alarm on long-chat route after yesterday's kernel swap. Not huge QPS change but p95 jumped from ~420ms to ~760ms. Anyone else seeing this pattern?
ryan: seeing it in traces. Kernel A -> Kernel B improved throughput for short messages, but long sequences have worse tail. suspect KV cache churn + larger microbatches.
micah: quick numbers from perf-run: kv hitrate on long-chat went 87% -> 62% after swap. median microbatch size increased 4 -> 8, and stealer latency spikes line up w/ cache misses.
anya: interesting — so batcher picks larger microbatches since Kernel B is faster per-token, but KV miss penalty kills p95. We need per-route token-budget targets that bias toward smaller batches for latency-sensitive routes.
ryan: agree. current queue policy is global token-budget per worker. we should try dynamic token budgets by route/tier: latency-tier routes get lower token budget (so earlier flush), throughput-tier keep larger.
micah: proposed quick experiment: add a route_tier map and do: 
```
route_tier:
  long-chat: latency
  embedding-bulk: throughput
batcher:
  default_token_budget: 512
  tier_overrides:
    latency: 256
    throughput: 1024
```
run canary on 5% of pods, compare p95 and token-econ.
anya: also want to test small change to queue policy: preempt a queued request if a latency-tier request arrives and current queue total tokens > route_budget. basically a light preemption gate.
ryan: preemption sounds good but be careful about starvation. simple rule: only preempt if queued > 2x route_budget and preempted requests are moved to head of worker queue after flush.
micah: added a small profiler output from one of the impacted hosts: 
```
host: gpu-23
kernel: B
samples: 1200
kv_hit: 62
kv_miss_tail_cost_ms: 95
avg_token_cost_ms: 1.9
microbatch_median: 8
p95_latency_ms: 760
```
infra-bot: deploy canary started for eng-runtime/batcher v2026.3-canary-07 -> 3 pods. Jenkins job #1421.
anya: can we also toggle kernel selection heuristic? maybe Kernel B should be chosen only for seq_len < 1024 on this hardware. Kernel selection + token budget together could fix tail.
ryan: good call. prob rule: if seq_len_est >= 1024 then prefer Kernel A (better KV locality), else Kernel B. We'll add that to the canary config.
micah: I'll run synthetic replay to simulate long-chat and measure kv eviction churn. local command: `./bin/batch-sim --profile=long-chat --concurrency=40 --seq=1500 --duration=5m`
anya: timeline: start canary with (1) tiered token budgets, (2) preemption gate, (3) kernel selection rule. monitor p95 and kv_hit in datadog. If p95 drops to <=480ms and kv_hit >80% on canary, promote.
ryan: adding dashboards: compare p95, avg_tokens_per_batch, kv_hit by route. Also add trace for preempt events.
micah: one more note — quantized model path increases kernel B speed but increases KV index page pressure (more memory churn). watch for GC/ooms.
anya: ack. let's run canary now. I pushed config to infra repo: `git rev a1b2c3f` and added canary tags.
ryan: thx. will watch. :eyes:
